record.original_question: If lambda_1, ..., lambda_n are linearly independent over Q and e^{lambda_1}, ..., e^{lambda_n} are algebraic, must lambda_1, ..., lambda_n be algebraically independent over Q?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.3 (Algebraic Independence of Logarithms of Algebraic Numbers). Let λ1 , . . . , λn be Q-linearly independent complex numbers. Assume that the numbers e^{λ1} , . . . , e^{λn} are algebraic. Then the numbers λ1 , . . . , λn are algebraically independent over Q.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $\lambda_1, \ldots, \lambda_n$ be complex numbers that are linearly independent over $\mathbb{Q}$, and assume that $e^{\lambda_1}, \ldots, e^{\lambda_n}$ are all algebraic numbers. Must $\lambda_1, \ldots, \lambda_n$ be algebraically independent over $\mathbb{Q}$?
artifact.status_search_result: This is the classical conjecture on algebraic independence of logarithms of algebraic numbers, widely attributed to Baker. It is a famous open problem in transcendence theory; only special cases (e.g., the Baker–Lindemann–Weierstrass results on linear independence of logarithms) are known. No proof of the full conjecture has been announced.

status_evidence.title: Conjecture on algebraic independence of logarithms (Waldschmidt)
status_evidence.snippet: The conjecture on algebraic independence of logarithms of algebraic numbers remains one of the main open problems in transcendence theory.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is widely cited as open.
